title: Gün sonu silently cancels a karaoke order whose room timer is running and closes the day
description: closeDay treats an open order with no items and no payments as an empty check: it sets the order to 'iptal' ('Boş adisyon (gün sonu)') and lets the day close. A karaoke order that has only a running room timer has no items yet, because the room charge is added only when the timer stops. So gün sonu cancels it, closes the day, and leaves the room_session running (endedAt null) on a cancelled order. The room charge can no longer be billed (stopRoom needs an open order), and the session is never closed.
evidence:
floor before gün sonu [ { ... itemCount: 0, source: 'pos', roomStartedAt: 1793028234992 } ]
gün sonu -> 200 closed
karaoke order after gün sonu { status: 'iptal', cancelReason: 'Boş adisyon (gün sonu)', room: { startedAt: 1793028234992, endedAt: null, hourlyRate: 100000 } }
AssertionError: expected 200 to be 409
fix: In the empty-order filter in closeDay, count an order with an active room session as non-empty (or call assertNoActiveRoom), so gün sonu reports it as an open order (room_running) instead of cancelling it.

votes.reason:
The bug reproduces on the current code. I wrote my own probe instead of reusing the claimant's: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-okanberkmanavoglu-Downloads/36639f88-6c66-4e9d-babe-a70914f282d6/scratchpad/audit/verify-state-r1-reproduce/dayclose-room-verify.probe.test.ts. To run only this probe, add the file filter `dayclose-room-verify` to the vitest command. Other agents' probes in the same folder fail for unrelated reasons.

What the probe does: opens the day, opens a masa order on the 'oda' table (hourlyRate 100000), calls room/start, then takes gün sonu. Output:
- Before gün sonu: status 'acik', 0 items, room {endedAt: null, hourlyRate: 100000}.
- Closing the order on the normal path is refused: `POST /orders/:id/close -> 409 room_running`. closeOrder and payment both call assertNoActiveRoom.
- `DAY CLOSE -> 200 closedAt set`. The day closes.
- After gün sonu: status 'iptal', cancelReason 'Boş adisyon (gün sonu)', total 0, room still {endedAt: null}.
- `room/stop after gün sonu -> 409 order_closed`. The room charge can no longer be billed.
- The room_sessions row is left with endedAt null and itemId null.
- The /floor entry for the room is now null, so staff no longer see that its timer is running.
- Audit log: room.start, then 'order.cancel: #1 boş adisyon gün sonunda kapatıldı' (severity info only), then 'day.close ... ciro ₺0,00'.
- The assertion `expect(close.status).toBe(409)` failed with "expected 200 to be 409".

Root cause: at server/services/days.ts:284 the empty-order filter in closeDay checks only orderItems and orderPayments. It does not check for an active room session. This is the one close path that skips the room_running guard used elsewhere (assertNoActiveRoom in server/services/orders.ts:78).

The damage cannot be undone in the app. reopenOrder (orders.ts:1011) accepts only 'kapali' orders, so the 'iptal' order can never be reopened. The room charge is lost silently.

The automatic gün sonu in server/jobs.ts:79 calls the same closeDay with actor null, so a forgotten timer is cancelled the same way at the automatic close.

Why medium and not the claimed high: it only triggers when the karaoke order has no items and no payments while its timer is still running at gün sonu. That is plausible (late session, or the automatic gün sonu) but narrow.

The proposed fix is sound: treat an order with an active room session as non-empty, so gün sonu refuses with open_orders or room_running.

Confirmed with my own probe: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-okanberkmanavoglu-Downloads/36639f88-6c66-4e9d-babe-a70914f282d6/scratchpad/audit/verify-state-r1-correctness/dayclose-room-verify.probe.test.ts. I ran only that file.

**What happens.** A karaoke room order has a running timer and no items yet. Gün sonu then:
- returns `gün sonu -> 200 { closedAt: true, zNo: 1 }`
- cancels the order: `after { status: 'iptal', cancelReason: 'Boş adisyon (gün sonu)', room: { startedAt: ..., endedAt: null, hourlyRate: 100000 } }`
- takes the room off the floor: `floor entry for room after none (room shows free)`
- blocks billing afterwards: `stopRoom after -> 409 order_closed`
- The test fails with `AssertionError: expected 200 to be 409`.

**Why the expected behaviour is correct.**
- In `server/services/days.ts` around line 282, the empty-order filter rests on the comment "Kalemsiz ve ödemesiz adisyon parasal iz bırakmaz" (an order with no items and no payments leaves no money trace). A running room session is unbilled revenue (rate 100000 kuruş per hour, minimum minutes apply), so it does leave a money trace.
- docs/02-PLAN.md describes this cleanup for counter orders only: "boş tezgâh adisyonu yeniden kullanılır, gün sonunda boşlar kapanır". It was not meant for room orders.
- The project already guards room charges elsewhere. `assertNoActiveRoom` (room_running) blocks `addPayment`, `closeOrder` and the cash-register (OKC) send. docs/02-PLAN.md and docs/04-YAZARKASA.md say a closed order must not take a room charge. tests/review-round2.test.ts covers "kapanmış adisyona oda ücreti yazılmaz" (no room charge on a closed order).

**Why the loss can't be recovered in-app.** `reopenOrder` reopens only `kapali` orders, never `iptal` ones, and only on the same open day. `stopRoom` requires an open order. So the room charge cannot be added to that order any more. The session row stays at `endedAt` null on a cancelled order. The only record is an info-level audit line, "#N boş adisyon gün sonunda kapatıldı".

**Why medium, not high.**
- Automatic gün sonu is not affected. `autoDayEndTick` in server/jobs.ts skips the close when any open POS order exists, even an empty one, so only a manual gün sonu cancels the order.
- It needs a fairly unusual situation: gün sonu taken while a room is in use, and the room order has no items.
- The cashier did see the room timer on the floor before closing.
- Staff could re-bill by hand with a new order and a manual price, which needs authorisation.

**Related gap.** `cancelOrder` has no `assertNoActiveRoom` either. My control test got `CTRL cancel 200 ... status iptal` for a running-timer order with no approval, while `closeOrder` correctly returned 409 room_running.

**Fix.** The proposed fix is sound: in the closeDay empty-order filter, treat an order with an active room session as non-empty, so gün sonu returns 409 (open_orders, or room_running from `assertNoActiveRoom`) instead of cancelling it.

Confirmed with a probe. A karaoke order with a running room timer and no items is cancelled when staff take gün sonu manually. The day then closes with no warning, and the room charge can no longer be billed.

- floor before [ { no: 1, itemCount: 0, roomStartedAt: true } ]
- gün sonu -> 200 closedAt set: true ... blind: true
- order after { status: 'iptal', cancelReason: 'Boş adisyon (gün sonu)', room: { endedAt: null, hourlyRate: 100000 } }
- audit: 'order.cancel [info] #1 boş adisyon gün sonunda kapatıldı' (no mention of the room or its running timer)
- stop room after gün sonu -> 409 order_closed; reopen order -> 409 'Yalnız kapanmış adisyon yeniden açılır'
- reopen day -> 200, then stop room -> 409 order_closed again, and reopen order -> 409 again. There is no way to recover the charge.
- floor after: room shows free

Control probe: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-okanberkmanavoglu-Downloads/36639f88-6c66-4e9d-babe-a70914f282d6/scratchpad/audit/verify-state-r1-impact/a-control.probe.test.ts (passes).
- The same room with one Latte is blocked: 409 open_orders 'Açık adisyon var: #1'.
- Stopping the timer adds 'Karaoke odası' 100000 kuruş ('1 sa', the 60-minute minimum).
- So each occurrence loses at least 1,000 TL in the demo settings, plus any further hours. That revenue never reaches the Z or lafmaliyet.

Impact: real lost or unbilled money, and staff are misled.
- The cashier relies on the open_orders guard, which works for orders with items.
- Here the response is a normal success, and the blind cashier only sees 'Gün kapandı'.
- The room vanishes from the floor, and the timer that holds the elapsed time is stuck on a cancelled order.
- The Z for that day understates sales, and recovering the charge means re-billing it by hand.

Why medium rather than high:
- It needs a specific sequence: a manual gün sonu while the karaoke room is occupied and the order has no items.
- The automatic gün sonu job skips when any open POS order exists, so only the manual path is affected.
- cancelOrder also lets staff explicitly cancel an empty order with a running timer, with no room check. That is a deliberate action, though, not a silent side effect of closing the day.
- No crash, data leak or permission bypass.

title: Moving all items out of a karaoke order, or cancelling it, orphans the running room timer
description: transferItems marks the source 'birlesti' once all its items have moved and it has no payments. Unlike mergeOrders, it does not move or check room_sessions, so a running timer stays attached to a merged order. stopRoom on the source fails with order_closed, and reopenOrder only accepts 'kapali', so the source cannot be reopened. The target has no timer, so it can be paid and closed without the room charge. cancelOrder has no assertNoActiveRoom either: cancelling a karaoke order leaves its session running forever.
fix: In transferItems, either call assertNoActiveRoom(source) before closing the source as 'birlesti', or move the active session to the target the way mergeOrders does. In cancelOrder, call assertNoActiveRoom, or end the session explicitly with an audit entry.

votes.reason:
Reproduced on the current code with my own probe: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-okanberkmanavoglu-Downloads/36639f88-6c66-4e9d-babe-a70914f282d6/scratchpad/audit/verify-state-r1-reproduce/room-orphan-verify.probe.test.ts. It runs with the given config, filtered to `room-orphan-verify`. Tests V1 to V3 fail their correct-behaviour assertions. V4, the merge control, passes.

**Code check**
- `transferItems` (server/services/orders.ts:609-680) sets the source to `birlesti` when no items and no payments are left (line 664-668). It never calls `assertNoActiveRoom` and never moves `room_sessions` to the target.
- `mergeOrders` (line 590) does move them.
- `cancelOrder` (line 1033) has no `assertNoActiveRoom`. Only `addPayment` and `closeOrder` call it.
- `stopRoom` (rooms.ts:44) needs the order to be `acik`. `reopenOrder` (line 1011) only accepts `kapali`.
- Nothing else in `server/` looks for running sessions, apart from `floorState`, which only reads open orders. So no day-close or other path can recover an orphaned session.
- tests/review-round2.test.ts treats "a closed order with a running timer" as a bad legacy state. So this is not intended behaviour.

**Probe output**
- V1 (all items moved to another table):
  - transfer 200; source `status: 'birlesti'` with `room { endedAt: null }`; target `{ status: 'acik', total: 14000, room: null }`.
  - Stopping the room on the source returns 409 `order_closed`. Reopening the source returns 409 "Yalnız kapanmış adisyon yeniden açılır".
  - `/floor` shows no running room timer anywhere (false).
  - Paying the target gives 200 `{ status: 'kapali', total: 14000, paid: 14000, items: ['Türk kahvesi'] }`, with no room charge. Afterwards the source session is still `[{ endedAt: null }]`.
- V2 (moved into an existing order via `targetOrderId`): same result. Source is `birlesti`, target room is null, and the session stays running.
- V3 (cancel): cancel returns 200 `iptal`; the session is still `[{ endedAt: null }]`. Stop then returns 409 `order_closed`.
- V4 (merge control): merge 200, the session moves to the target, and stop returns 200 with total 114000. That total includes the 100000-kuruş minimum room charge, which the transfer path loses.

**Severity**
Medium fits. Using ordinary actions (transfer needs `masa.islem`, cancel needs `siparis.iptal`), staff can close or cancel a karaoke order and skip the room charge. The session is left orphaned and running, cannot be stopped or recovered, and does not show on the floor. The fix proposed in the claim is sound: either refuse with `assertNoActiveRoom`, or move or end the session the way `mergeOrders` does.

The bug is real. My probe reproduces both paths, and the cancel path is worse than the claim says.

**Why the claimed expected behaviour is correct.** The project clearly means a running room timer to always end up billed:
- addPayment, closeOrder and OKC send all call assertNoActiveRoom (server/services/orders.ts:78, 823, 948).
- mergeOrders moves room_sessions to the target (orders.ts:590).
- moveOrder carries the active session's tableId with it (orders.ts:569).
- tests/review-round2.test.ts:160 and tests/api-flow.test.ts:146 check that you cannot pay or close while the timer runs.

Two functions skip this guard:
- transferItems (orders.ts:618-680) marks the source 'birlesti' once it is empty and unpaid, without moving or checking room_sessions.
- cancelOrder (orders.ts:1033) has no assertNoActiveRoom check.

Nothing documents this as intentional.

**Probe:** /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-okanberkmanavoglu-Downloads/36639f88-6c66-4e9d-babe-a70914f282d6/scratchpad/audit/verify-state-r1-correctness/room-orphan.probe.test.ts. Each scenario backdates the timer to a 3-hour run at hourlyRate 100000 kuruş (₺1.000 per hour). Two tests fail.

**Scenario A: transfer.** The garson does it directly with masa.islem, no approver PIN. Output:
- `A transfer status 200`
- `A source after transfer { status: 'birlesti', room: { ..., endedAt: null, hourlyRate: 100000 } }`
- `A target after transfer { status: 'acik', total: 14000, room: null }`
- `A floor on room table (free)`
- `A stop on source 409 { code: 'order_closed' }`
- `A stop on target 404 not_found`
- `A reopen source 409 'Yalnız kapanmış adisyon yeniden açılır'`
- `A target paid { closed: true, total: 14000, roomHoursBilled: 0 }`
- `A new order on same room, start timer 200`
- `A running sessions on room table 3` (orphaned sessions pile up)

**Scenario B: cancel.** The garson cancels an order that has only a running timer, with no PIN and an empty reason. Output:
- `B payment while running 409 room_running` and `B close while running 409 room_running` (the intended guards work here)
- `B cancel by garson, no pin, no reason 200 iptal room in dto: { endedAt: null, hourlyRate: 100000 }`
- `B sessions [ { endedAt: null, itemId: null } ]`
- `B audit [ room.start info, order.cancel severity 'info' approverId null message '#1 boş adisyon kapatıldı' ]`

The room charge only becomes an order item when the timer stops. So a karaoke order with no other items counts as "empty": cancelOrder needs no siparis.iptal approval and no reason, and logs it as an info-level "boş adisyon kapatıldı". This lets staff run the room for hours, cancel without approval, and take payment off the books, while payment and close stay correctly blocked. That conflicts with the AGENTS.md rule that sensitive actions are audited, and with the project's anti-theft intent (blind cash). The transfer path loses the same revenue silently, without approval.

**Severity.** Raised from medium to high because the room charge is lost without approval and under a misleading audit entry.

**Fix.** The proposed fix is right:
- In transferItems, call assertNoActiveRoom on the source before marking it 'birlesti', or move the session to the target as mergeOrders does.
- In cancelOrder, call assertNoActiveRoom, or end the session with an approval-gated audit entry.

Confirmed: this loses room revenue silently and gets around the server's own "room_running" payment guard.

Probe: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-okanberkmanavoglu-Downloads/36639f88-6c66-4e9d-babe-a70914f282d6/scratchpad/audit/verify-state-r1-impact/room-orphan-impact.probe.test.ts (2 of 3 tests fail as expected; the control test passes). Each test pushes the room session's startedAt back by 3 hours.

Control (normal path): with the timer running, payment is refused with room_running (addPayment and closeOrder both call assertNoActiveRoom). Stopping the timer bills the room. The audit row reads "room.stop: Oda sayacı durdu: 195 dk, ₺3.250,00 adisyona eklendi".

Impact 1, transfer (orders.ts:664):
- A garson moves the only item to another table with "Hesabı böl / kalem taşı". The garson has masa.islem, so no approval is asked; the modal allows selecting every item.
- Output: source { status: 'birlesti', room: true }, target { status: 'acik', room: null, total: 14000 }.
- The /floor view no longer lists the room table ("none (room shows free)").
- Paying the target returns 200: status kapali, paid 14000. The roughly ₺3,000+ room charge is never billed.
- The orphan session stays { endedAt: null, itemId: null, hoursRunning: 3 }.
- Stopping the timer on the source returns 409 order_closed. Reopening the source returns 409 "Yalnız kapanmış adisyon yeniden açılır", so the charge cannot be recovered.
- The audit trail shows only "info order.transfer: #2 adisyondan 1 kalem #3 adisyona taşındı". There is no room.stop and no void.
- mergeOrders moves room_sessions to the target; transferItems does not. The guard the project deliberately added is bypassed.

Impact 2, cancel (orders.ts:1033):
- A kasiyer, whose role lacks siparis.iptal, cancels a karaoke order that has no items but a timer that has run 3 hours.
- Result: 200 iptal, with no approval. The audit row is severity 'info', amount 0, "#4 boş adisyon kapatıldı". The session stays at endedAt null.
- Control: if the same order's timer is stopped first, the same cashier's cancel returns 403 approval_required.
- So a running timer lets a 3-hour room session be written off as an "empty check", with no approval and a misleading audit entry.
- This part is weaker on its own: a dishonest cashier could also simply never start the timer.

What it does not affect:
- The Z report is not blocked. Day close and reports never read room_sessions.
- The orphan row does not crash anything; it shows up only as a stale "running" room on the dead order's DTO.

Severity: medium. Moving every item out of a karaoke order is less common than "Masa taşı", which correctly carries the timer, but it is reachable in the UI with no warning. It silently loses a real charge (₺1,000/h in the demo data) and leaves staff and the audit log with no sign of it.

title: Room timer can start while the bill is on the fiscal device; the device payment then closes the order with the timer running
description: sendOrderToDevice refuses to send while a room timer runs (assertNoActiveRoom), but startRoom does not check for a pending device basket. If the timer starts after the basket is sent, the device payment (addExternalPayments, line 1202) closes the order because total - paid <= 0, with no active-room check. The order ends 'kapali' with a running timer, stopRoom returns order_closed, and the room time is billed only if a manager reopens the order.
fix: Call assertNoPendingDevice in startRoom (export it from orders.ts). In addExternalPayments, do not close the order while an active room session exists: record the payment, leave the order open, and emit an alert.

votes.reason:
I reproduced the bug on the current code with my own probe: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-okanberkmanavoglu-Downloads/36639f88-6c66-4e9d-babe-a70914f282d6/scratchpad/audit/verify-state-r1-reproduce/room-device-repro.probe.test.ts (run with a "room-device-repro" filter).

**Control test (passes):** the code already enforces "no device send while a room timer runs". POST /okc/orders/:id/send returns 409 while the timer runs, because of assertNoActiveRoom at server/okc/service.ts:106. addPayment (orders.ts:823) and closeOrder (orders.ts:948) apply the same guard.

**Repro test (fails):**
1. I sent the karaoke-room order's basket to the simulator: amount 142000.
2. POST /orders/:id/room/start returned **200** while the basket was still pending. startRoom (server/services/rooms.ts:25) has no assertNoPendingDevice check.
3. The simulator payment (POST /okc/simulator/baskets/:id/pay) returned 200 with status 'tamamlandi'. That path runs applySale and then addExternalPayments (orders.ts:1124), which closes the order once total - paid <= 0 and never checks for an active room.
4. The order afterwards was status 'kapali', total 142000, paid 142000, with room { startedAt: 1793028956666, endedAt: null, hourlyRate: 100000 }.
5. POST /room/stop then returned 409 with code 'order_closed' ("Adisyon kapalı; oda ücretini yazmak için önce adisyonu yeniden açın").
6. The assertion "startRoom should be refused while a basket is pending on the device: expected 200 not to be 200" failed.

**Impact:** the order closes with the room timer still running, which breaks the rule the code enforces on every other close path. The room-time charge (minimum 100000 kuruş/hour here) goes unbilled unless someone notices and reopens the order. Medium severity is fair. The fix should be assertNoPendingDevice in startRoom, and/or no auto-close in addExternalPayments while a room session is active.

Confirmed by my own probe at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-okanberkmanavoglu-Downloads/36639f88-6c66-4e9d-babe-a70914f282d6/scratchpad/audit/verify-state-r1-correctness/room-device.probe.test.ts. To run only this file, filter on "room-device.probe", because the folder also holds other verifiers' probes.

The claimed expected behaviour matches what the project intends. Every other way of closing an order refuses while a room timer runs:
- addPayment (orders.ts:823) and closeOrder (orders.ts:948) call assertNoActiveRoom.
- sendOrderToDevice calls it too (okc/service.ts:106), with the comment "Oda sayacı çalışırken hesap kapanmaz: cihazda ödenen adisyona sonradan oda ücreti yazılırdı" (the bill must not close while the timer runs, or the room fee gets written onto a bill already paid on the device).
- docs/02-PLAN.md says "oda sayacı çalışırken hesap cihaza gitmez, kapanmış adisyona oda ücreti yazılmaz" (a running timer keeps the bill off the device; no room fee goes onto a closed bill).
- tests/review-round2.test.ts treats a closed order with a running timer as legacy bad data ("Eski veride…").

The gap has two parts:
- startRoom (rooms.ts:25) does not check for a pending device basket.
- addExternalPayments (orders.ts:1202) closes the order when total - paid <= 0 without checking for an active room.

The UI does not block it either. The Başlat (start) button in OrderPage.tsx is shown whenever `editable` is true, and `editable` ignores a pending basket. So a waiter on a handheld can start the timer while the cashier's basket waits on the device, for example in "masada ödeme" (pay-at-table) list mode.

Probe output:
- Control: cash payment with the timer running returns 409 room_running, and so does a device send.
- Bug path:
  - A garson (waiter) calls room/start while the basket is pending: 200.
  - After the simulated device payment, the order is status 'kapali' (closed), total 28000, paid 28000, with room endedAt null.
  - The /floor entry for the room table is null. The floor only lists open orders, so the running timer disappears from the floor plan.
  - room/stop then returns 409 order_closed.
  - The assertion that an order never ends closed with a running timer fails (expected true to be false).

Impact: the hourly room charge (seed rate 1000 TL/h) is silently lost. It can only be recovered if someone notices and a person with odeme.iade reopens the order on the same business day; reopenOrder refuses an order from an earlier day. After that the session stays orphaned for good.

The sequence (start the timer after the full bill was sent to the device) is unusual but reachable through the normal UI and API, so medium severity is fair.

Partial-item baskets do not trigger it, because the order stays open while total - paid > 0.

The bug is real and it loses money. My probe shows the room charge can go unbilled with no warning, and after the Z it cannot be billed through the system at all. I wrote my own probe and did not change any repo files.

Probe: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-okanberkmanavoglu-Downloads/36639f88-6c66-4e9d-babe-a70914f282d6/scratchpad/audit/verify-state-r1-impact/room-device-impact.probe.test.ts (run with the vitest.probe.config.mts in the same folder, filter "room-device-impact").

**Control (passes):** starting the room timer first and then sending to the device is refused with 409 room_running. So the design does mean to stop a room order from being paid at the device while the timer runs. Only the reverse order slips through: rooms.ts:25 startRoom never calls assertNoPendingDevice.

**Bug path output:**
- room/start while the basket is pending returns 200. The floor shows the order with roomStartedAt set.
- After the device payment, the order reads: status 'kapali', total 28000, paid 28000, room endedAt null, hourlyRate 100000. addExternalPayments closes the order because total minus paid is 0 or less, and it does not check for a running room.
- The floor entry for the room table becomes null. floorState only loads 'acik' orders, so the running timer disappears from the floor and the room looks free.
- room/stop returns 409 order_closed.
- A new order on the same room returns 200.
- Day close (Z) with the timer still running returns 200. closeDay checks only for open orders, not running timers, and logs no alarm.
- Reopening the order after the Z returns 409 day_closed. The final order is still 'kapali' with paid 28000 and a timer that never stops.

**Impact:**
- The whole room charge is lost (1,000 TL per hour on the demo karaoke room).
- The closed order keeps showing "Oda açık" with a running clock, which misleads staff.
- The Z under-reports revenue for the room.
- The charge can only be recovered if a manager reopens the order before the Z.

**Why staff would hit it:** the client shows the Başlat (start) button whenever the order is editable, even while a basket is waiting on the device. The server already refuses to send to the device while the timer runs, so "pay for the drinks first, then start the room" is the natural order. In the table-side payment mode the basket can wait a long time, which makes the gap easy to hit.

**Why medium, not higher:** staff must start the timer during that pending window, and a manager can still fix it by reopening before the Z.

title: Automatic gün sonu is blocked by the empty orders that gün sonu itself auto-cancels (e.g. the empty 'Yeni satış' tezgâh check)
description: autoDayEndTick skips the close if any open POS order exists for the day, and logs 'Otomatik gün sonu alınamadı: N açık adisyon var'. closeDay treats item-less, payment-less orders as harmless and cancels them (days.ts 281-288). The cashier screen opens an empty tezgâh order after every sale (OrderPage.nextSale), and tapping a free table creates an empty masa order. So at night there is normally at least one empty open order, and the automatic day end never runs. The same state closes fine by hand, and the control probe shows the tick closes the day when no open order exists.
fix: In autoDayEndTick, apply the same filter as closeDay (ignore orders with no items and no payments, and include running room sessions per the gün sonu finding), or just attempt closeDay and catch the open_orders conflict to log the skip.

The bug reproduces on the current code. I wrote my own probes in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-okanberkmanavoglu-Downloads/36639f88-6c66-4e9d-babe-a70914f282d6/scratchpad/audit/verify-state-r1-reproduce (a-tezgah.probe.test.ts, b-masa.probe.test.ts, c-control.probe.test.ts, common.ts). They do not reuse the original probe. Each one turns on autoDayEnd at hour 3 and opens the day at 18:00 Istanbul time. It then sets the clock to 03:00:30 and runs the real startJobs() timers for about 125 s.

Results (probe.log):
- A, empty tezgâh order: a paid counter sale is followed by the POST /orders {type:'tezgah'} that OrderPage.nextSale() makes. The database then holds [{sale, kapali, 14000}, {next, acik, total 0}]. After the auto tick: {"days":[{"closed":false}],"skips":["Otomatik gün sonu alınamadı: 1 açık adisyon var"],"closes":[],"cashDayOpen":true}, and the empty order is still acik. A manual POST /cash/day/close on the same state returns 200 and cancels that order (status iptal, "Boş adisyon (gün sonu)").
- B, empty masa order: the same thing happens when a free table is tapped (FloorPage.tapTable creates an order with no items). The auto tick is skipped with "1 açık adisyon var", while the manual close returns 200 and cancels the empty order.
- C, control: with no open order the tick closes the day: "Otomatik gün sonu alındı (Z 1): ciro ₺140,00".

Root cause: autoDayEndTick (server/jobs.ts lines 69-77) counts every acik POS order. closeDay (server/services/days.ts lines 281-288) cancels orders that have no items and no payments, so they never block a manual close. createOrder reuses an empty tezgâh order, but only one per cashier. One empty "next sale" therefore always stays open after the last counter sale. So when auto gün sonu is on, it never runs in normal counter use, and the day stays open until someone closes it by hand. Sales after 05:00 then fall into the wrong Z, which breaks the one-Z-per-business-date rule.

Medium fits: autoDayEnd is an opt-in setting (off by default), a day.auto_skip warning is written to the audit log, a manual close still works, and no money is miscounted.

Confirmed. The project says in three places that empty checks should never block gün sonu, but the automatic tick only checks for open orders, so these empty checks stop it.

Stated intent:
- server/services/orders.ts:177-178 reuses the empty tezgâh check so that "boşlar birikip gün sonunu tutmasın".
- closeDay (server/services/days.ts:281-288) says "Kalemsiz ve ödemesiz adisyon parasal iz bırakmaz: gün sonunu tutmaz, kendiliğinden kapanır". It cancels such checks as 'Boş adisyon (gün sonu)'.
- docs/02-PLAN.md says "satış bitince yeni satış; boş tezgâh adisyonu yeniden kullanılır, gün sonunda boşlar kapanır".

The bug: autoDayEndTick (server/jobs.ts:69-77) counts every order with status 'acik' and source 'pos', without that filter. The client always leaves such a check open:
- OrderPage.nextSale (src/pages/order/OrderPage.tsx:131, called at :386 after every tezgâh payment) POSTs a new empty tezgâh order.
- FloorPage (src/pages/FloorPage.tsx:50) creates a masa order as soon as a free table is tapped.
So after the last counter sale of the night there is always one empty open check, and the opt-in automatic gün sonu never runs in the main tezgâh workflow.

Docs/01-ANALIZ.md describes the feature as closing the day "açık adisyon yoksa". That reads as checks holding money, which matches closeDay's own rule. It is not a deliberate choice to let empty checks block.

Independent probes in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-okanberkmanavoglu-Downloads/36639f88-6c66-4e9d-babe-a70914f282d6/scratchpad/audit/verify-state-r1-correctness/. Each starts the real startJobs timer at 06:00:30 with autoDayEnd on, hour 6, and the day opened at 20:00 the evening before.

  - Manual close on the same state: '[tezgah] manual close same state 200 {"emptyOrder":"iptal","cancelReason":"Boş adisyon (gün sonu)"}'.
- vfy-autodayend-masa.probe.test.ts (FAIL, empty check left after tapping table S1)
  - '[masa] after 06:00 auto tick {"dayClosed":false,"skips":["Otomatik gün sonu alınamadı: 1 açık adisyon var"],"openOrders":[{"no":1,"type":"masa","total":0,"paid":0}]}'
- vfy-autodayend-control.probe.test.ts (PASS, same sale with no empty check)
  - '[control] after 06:00 auto tick {"dayClosed":true,"note":"Otomatik gün sonu"}'
- Full log: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-okanberkmanavoglu-Downloads/36639f88-6c66-4e9d-babe-a70914f282d6/scratchpad/audit/verify-state-r1-correctness/vfy-autodayend.log

Impact:
- When the day is not closed, getOpenDay keeps returning it, so the next day's sales go into the previous business day's Z. Preventing that is the whole point of the feature.
- Severity stays medium, not high:
  - autoDayEnd is off by default (server/lib/settings.ts:67).
  - Each skip writes a 'day.auto_skip' warning to the audit log.
  - No money is computed wrongly.
  - A manual gün sonu works.

The proposed fix is sound: apply closeDay's filter for checks with no items and no payments (or call closeDay and treat the open_orders 409 as a skip).

Confirmed with my own probe. The claim holds, and it causes a real reporting error, not just a skipped convenience.

Code path: autoDayEndTick (server/jobs.ts:69) skips the close if any open POS order exists, empty ones included. closeDay (server/services/days.ts ~281-288) cancels item-less, payment-less orders as harmless. createOrder (server/services/orders.ts:176-185) has a comment saying empty tezgâh orders must not "hold up gün sonu". OrderPage.nextSale (src/pages/order/OrderPage.tsx:131, called from PaymentModal onDone at :386) POSTs a new tezgâh order after every closed counter sale. So the normal cashier flow always leaves one empty open order overnight, and the auto close never runs.

Impact probe: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-okanberkmanavoglu-Downloads/36639f88-6c66-4e9d-babe-a70914f282d6/scratchpad/audit/verify-state-r1-impact/autodayend-impact.probe.test.ts

Scenario: auto gün sonu on at 06:00. Day opened 27 Ekim 20:00, one cash sale, then the nextSale empty order. Tick at 28 Ekim 06:05. Another sale at 28 Ekim 12:00.
- [bug] after 06:05 auto tick {"day1Date":"2026-10-27","day1Closed":false,"autoSkip":["Otomatik gün sonu alınamadı: 1 açık adisyon var"]}
- [bug] 12:00 next day, kasa sees day {"date":"2026-10-27","zNo":1,"closed":false}
- [bug] sale made on 28 Ekim 12:00 {"total":28000,"attributedToBusinessDate":"2026-10-27","zNo":1}
- [bug] summary report {"report_2026_10_27":{"netSales":42000,"receipts":2},"report_2026_10_28":{"netSales":0,"receipts":0}}
- AssertionError: expected '2026-10-27' to be '2026-10-28'

Control (same flow without the empty order): the day auto-closes. The 28 Ekim sale goes to Z 2 dated 2026-10-28, and the reports split correctly: 27 Ekim = 14000, 28 Ekim = 28000.

This breaks the one-Z-per-business-date rule, and those per-date figures also feed lafmaliyet. The audit warning tells staff there is "1 açık adisyon" when no real open check exists, which is misleading.

No money is lost: totals are complete, only filed under the wrong date. The feature is off by default, and a manual gün sonu works and cleans up the empty order. That keeps the severity at medium rather than high.

title: Voiding a fresh, never-prepared item does not release its limited portion: the product stays sold out on POS and the site
description: addItems decrements products.portionsLeft and sets active=false at 0 (and pushes availability.push to laffogato). voidItem and cancelOrder never add the portion back, even for a fresh void within the grace window (status 'yeni', never started, so nothing was made). Entering the last portion by mistake and voiding it at once leaves the product 'tükendi' on the POS and on the website until a manager edits portions by hand.
evidence:
fresh void -> 200
product after void { active: false, portionsLeft: 0 }
selling the still-uneaten portion -> 409 sold_out Türk kahvesi tükendi
AssertionError: expected 409 to be 200
fix: When voiding (at least fresh, not-after-send voids) or cancelling items of a product with portionsLeft != null, add the qty back in the same transaction, set active=true if it was 0, and emit menu/availability events.

votes.reason:
The bug reproduces on the current code. I wrote my own probe instead of reusing the claimed one: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-okanberkmanavoglu-Downloads/36639f88-6c66-4e9d-babe-a70914f282d6/scratchpad/audit/verify-state-r1-reproduce/portions-release.probe.test.ts. To run only this file: npx vitest run --config .../verify-state-r1-reproduce/vitest.probe.config.mts portions-release. The shared directory also holds other verifiers' probes.

Test A covers the item void path. It sets Türk kahvesi to 1 portion, the cashier sells it, and the item is status 'yeni' with startedAt null. Output:
- "A after sale { active: false, portionsLeft: 0 }"
- "A void status 200 item voided true" (a fresh void inside the grace window, no approval)
- "A after fresh void { active: false, portionsLeft: 0 }"
- "A re-sell -> 409 sold_out Türk kahvesi tükendi"

Both assertions of the correct behaviour fail: the product should be { active: true, portionsLeft: 1 } and the re-sell should return 200.

Test B covers the order cancel path, which the claim also names. It sets 3 portions, sells 2 (fresh), then cancels the order. Output: "B after sale { active: true, portionsLeft: 1 }", "B cancel status 200 iptal", "B after fresh cancel { active: true, portionsLeft: 1 }". The assertion of portionsLeft 3 fails, so cancelling never gives portions back either.

The code agrees with the probe:
- addItems (server/services/orders.ts:276-283) decrements portionsLeft and sets active=false at 0. It then emits menu product.sold_out and sync availability.push, which marks the product sold out on the laffogato site.
- voidItem (lines 329-372) and cancelOrder (lines 1033-1069) never touch products.portionsLeft or active, and emit no menu or availability event. grep finds no other code that adds portions back.

This holds even for a 'fresh' void, where the code itself records that nothing was started or made (fresh=true, voidAfterSend=false). The product stays 'tükendi' on the POS and the site until a manager edits portions by hand through PATCH /admin/products or toggles availability.

Medium fits: no money or permission impact and a manual workaround exists, but it wrongly blocks sales on both POS and site. That breaks the documented "porsiyon sayacı" (portion counter) behaviour, under which a product goes sold out only when its portions are actually used up.

The behaviour is confirmed, but the impact is smaller than claimed. It only affects stock state. It does not touch money, the Z, reports, permissions, data or server stability.

Code: in server/services/orders.ts, addItems (lines 276-283) lowers products.portionsLeft, sets active=false when it reaches 0 and emits availability.push. voidItem (line 329) and cancelOrder (line 1033) never give the portion back. This holds even for a "fresh" void (status 'yeni', never started, same user, inside VOID_GRACE_MS), which is the flow built for fixing a wrong tap.

Probe: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-okanberkmanavoglu-Downloads/36639f88-6c66-4e9d-babe-a70914f282d6/scratchpad/audit/verify-state-r1-impact/portions-impact.probe.test.ts (all 3 tests fail):
- A (last portion): "void 200 after { active: false, portionsLeft: 0 }" and then "sell remaining portion -> 409 sold_out Matcha Latte tükendi".
- B (counter 3, fresh void of 1): "after fresh void { active: true, portionsLeft: 2 }" and then "sold 2 -> 200 ; 3rd real portion -> 409 sold_out". The counter drifts with no visible sign, and the product sells out while a portion is still on hand.
- C (fresh whole-order cancel of 2 out of 2): "cancel 200 after { active: false, portionsLeft: 0 }".

Real-world effect: staff see 'tükendi' on the POS while portions remain, so sales are lost. The website also gets the sold-out push and shows the item as sold out. Fresh voids of mistaken items are a normal, frequent flow, so this is not just theoretical.

Why the claim is overstated: it does not need "a manager editing portions by hand". A cashier with urun.tukendi (on by default for kasiyer) can reopen the item from the POS 'Tükenen ürünler' dialog. The probe shows "cashier reopen -> 200 ... after reopen { active: true, portionsLeft: null }". That reopen sets the counter to null (unlimited), so the limit is lost and the item can then be oversold. Case B, where the counter drifts by one with no sign, has no recovery short of someone noticing.

Rating: real but low. It is an operational inventory and availability error, not a money, Z-report or security problem.

Confirmed with a probe. The claimed expected behaviour is right for a café POS, and nothing in the project says otherwise.

What the code does: addItems (server/services/orders.ts:276-283) takes qty off products.portionsLeft. When the count reaches 0 it sets active=false and emits menu product.sold_out plus sync availability.push, which pushSoldOut sends to laffogato as isActive:false. voidItem (orders.ts:329) and cancelOrder (orders.ts:1033) never touch products, so the portions are not given back. That holds even for a "fresh" void: status 'yeni', never started, same user, within VOID_GRACE_MS. The code already treats that case as a harmless mistake (no approval, severity info, voidAfterSend=false), so nothing was made and the portion is still there to sell.

Why the expected behaviour is right: the counter is meant to track "günlük adet, sıfırda otomatik Tükendi (ve siteye bildirim)" (docs/02-PLAN.md:103), so it should match what is actually left to sell. No doc, test or AGENTS.md rule says a void should keep a portion used up. Grepping tests/ and docs/ finds nothing about voids and portions.

Probe: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-okanberkmanavoglu-Downloads/36639f88-6c66-4e9d-babe-a70914f282d6/scratchpad/audit/verify-state-r1-correctness/portions-void-verify.probe.test.ts
Output:
A (last portion, fresh void): "A after add { active: false, portionsLeft: 0 } item status yeni" / "A void status 200" / "A after fresh void { active: false, portionsLeft: 0 }" / "A resell 409 sold_out Türk kahvesi tükendi".
B (5 portions, add 2, fresh void): "B after fresh void of 2 { active: true, portionsLeft: 3 }", expected 5. The count drifts with no warning, so the item will show sold out too early later.
C (2 portions, add 2, fresh cancelOrder): "C after fresh cancel { active: false, portionsLeft: 0 }".
D (the one-tap fix a cashier with urun.tukendi can use, POST /sync/products/:id/availability active=true): "D after satisa ac { active: true, portionsLeft: null }". setAvailability (laffogato-orders.ts:213) turns the counter off, so this fix ends portion tracking. The other fix is a manager re-entering the count in Yönetim. That admin PATCH sets active=true only in LafPOS and pushes nothing to the site.

Severity: medium is fair, at the lower end. There is no money, KDV, permission or report damage. But a limited item wrongly shows sold out on the POS and on the website (lost sales), and in case B the count drifts silently.

Scope of the fix: give back qty only for voids or cancels of items never started (status 'yeni', no startedAt), at least the fresh ones. Prepared or after-send voids are real waste and should not restore. Do it in the same transaction, set active=true when the count goes from 0 back above 0, emit menu product.available, and push isActive:true to the site, because pushSoldOut only sends false today.

title: Running karaoke room charge is lost when the itemless order is cancelled (any role, no approval) or auto-cancelled at day close
description: cancelOrder does not call assertNoActiveRoom. An order whose only billable content is a running room timer has no live items, so the cancel needs no approval, no reason and no permission check: even the bar-screen (mutfak) user can do it. The audit entry is 'boş adisyon kapatıldı' at info level. closeDay (server/services/days.ts:283-287) does the same thing automatically: it treats an order with no items and no payments as empty and sets it to 'iptal', even while its room session is still running. In both cases the session stays open on an 'iptal' order, and stopRoom then refuses with 409 order_closed, so the hourly charge (at least 60 min x 1000 TL in the seed) can never be billed. closeOrder, addPayment and sendOrderToDevice all guard against a running room; cancel and the day-close auto-cancel do not.
evidence:
bar cancel status 200 iptal total 0
after cancel: status iptal room { id: '01M5WCT863VHPTQQ4N5RVN18BE', startedAt: 1793028071619, endedAt: null, hourlyRate: 100000 } total 0
stop after cancel: 409 {"error":"Adisyon kapalı; oda ücretini yazmak için önce adisyonu yeniden açın","code":"order_closed"}
--- day close: 200 ...
order after day close: status iptal cancelReason Boş adisyon (gün sonu) total 0
fix: In cancelOrder, call assertNoActiveRoom(t, orderId) and require needDirect(actor,'siparis.al') even when the order is empty. In closeDay, treat an order with an open room_sessions row as not empty: list it in openPos and block the Z.

votes.reason:
The bug reproduces on the current code. I wrote my own probes and ran them in a fresh in-process database:
- /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-okanberkmanavoglu-Downloads/36639f88-6c66-4e9d-babe-a70914f282d6/scratchpad/audit/verify-money-r1-reproduce/room-cancel.probe.test.ts
- /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-okanberkmanavoglu-Downloads/36639f88-6c66-4e9d-babe-a70914f282d6/scratchpad/audit/verify-money-r1-reproduce/room-dayclose.probe.test.ts

The config is vitest.probe.config.mts in the same directory. No repo files were changed.

**Control (normal path):** starting the room and then stopping it bills the minimum hour: "[control] stopped total kurus = 100000 hourlyRate = 100000" (1,000 TL).

**Cancel path:** the bar screen user (role mutfak) has no order permissions. It gets 403 on room/stop and on adding items, with permission siparis.al. Closing the order while the room timer runs is correctly blocked with 409 room_running. But a cancel by that same bar user goes through:
- "[bug] bar cancel: 200 status= iptal total= 0 room= {...endedAt:null,hourlyRate:100000}"
- The room_sessions row stays open: "[ { endedAt: null, itemId: null, hourlyRate: 100000 } ]".
- The audit is only "order.cancel/info: #2 boş adisyon kapatıldı". There is no approver and no reason.
- Stopping the room afterwards fails with "409 ... order_closed".
- Reopening the order is also refused, even by patron: "409 Yalnız kapanmış adisyon yeniden açılır", because reopenOrder only accepts status 'kapali'.

So the room charge is lost for good. The cause is in cancelOrder (server/services/orders.ts:1033). It never calls assertNoActiveRoom. With no live items, approverId is null, no reason is required, and the route has no permission gate (server/routes/pos.ts:242-247).

**Day-close path:** closing the day returns 200 and closes Z 1 ("zNo":1, closedAt set). The order ends up as "status iptal cancelReason Boş adisyon (gün sonu) total 0", while the room still shows endedAt:null. A later room/stop gets "409 ... order_closed". The cause is in closeDay (server/services/days.ts:283-287): an order counts as empty when it has no items and no payments, and room_sessions are not checked.

This breaks the project rules: billable money disappears without an approval or a meaningful audit, and a role without siparis.* permissions can trigger it. The minimum loss is 1,000 TL per occurrence in the seed data, and it cannot be recovered, so high severity is justified.

Confirmed with a probe that fails on the correct-behaviour assertion. Probe: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-okanberkmanavoglu-Downloads/36639f88-6c66-4e9d-babe-a70914f282d6/scratchpad/audit/verify-money-r1-correctness/room-cancel.probe.test.ts. Both tests fail.

**Cause in the code**
- `cancelOrder` (`server/services/orders.ts:1033`) asks for approval and a reason only when the order has live items (`live.length`). It never calls `assertNoActiveRoom`, and for an itemless order it checks no permission at all.
- `closeDay` (`server/services/days.ts:283-287`) treats an order with no items and no payments as empty and marks it 'iptal' without looking at `room_sessions`.
- `reopenOrder` only reopens orders with status 'kapali', so an 'iptal' order can never come back.
- `stopRoom` refuses any order that is not 'acik' (409 order_closed).
- `floorState` only reads room sessions of open orders, so the room shows as free while the old session never ends.

**Probe output**
- The room table is "Karaoke odası" at hourlyRate 100000 (1.000 TL).
- The bar user has no `siparis.al` permission. `room/stop` by bar returns 403 forbidden `siparis.al`, yet `/cancel` by bar with an empty reason returns 200 'iptal'.
- After the cancel the order is 'iptal', total 0, and the room session is still open (`endedAt: null`, hourlyRate 100000).
- Stopping the room afterwards returns 409 `{"code":"order_closed"}`. Reopening the order with mudur approval returns 409 "Yalnız kapanmış adisyon yeniden açılır".
- The floor shows nothing on the room table.
- The only audit rows are `order.cancel` at info level ("#1 boş adisyon kapatıldı") and `room.start`.
- Day close by kasa returns 200 Z. The order becomes 'iptal' with "Boş adisyon (gün sonu)", total 0 and the room still running; stopping the room then returns 409 order_closed.
- The automatic day-end job (`server/jobs.ts:69-77`) skips when any order is open, so only a manual Z cancels the order. The claim's day-close path is still correct.

**Why it is a bug, not intended**
- docs/02-PLAN.md and docs/04-YAZARKASA.md describe the room timer as billable. They say the bill does not go to the device while the timer runs (`room_running`) and that a room charge is not written to a closed order unless it is reopened.
- `closeOrder`, `addPayment` and the device send (okc) all call `assertNoActiveRoom`.
- The "empty order" rule ("Kalemsiz ve ödemesiz adisyon parasal iz bırakmaz") assumes the order leaves no money behind. A running hourly room breaks that assumption.
- This goes against the AGENTS.md rules that permissions are enforced server-side and sensitive actions are audited. A role without `siparis.al` can cancel the order, and a 1.000 TL/hour charge disappears with an info-level audit, no approval, no reason and no way to recover it.
- It is also a fraud path: take cash for the room, cancel the "empty" order, and blind cash hides the gap.

**Proposed fix (sound)**
- In `cancelOrder`, call `assertNoActiveRoom` and require `siparis.al`.
- In `closeDay`, count an open room session as non-empty so the order blocks the Z.

The bug is real: an order whose only charge is a running room timer can be cancelled with no approval, and the charge is then lost for good. Probe: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-okanberkmanavoglu-Downloads/36639f88-6c66-4e9d-babe-a70914f282d6/scratchpad/audit/verify-money-r1-impact/room-cancel-impact.probe.test.ts (3 tests, 2 fail on the correct-behaviour assertions; baseline lines are in room-cancel-baseline.log in the same folder).

Baseline (correct control): after the timer runs about 2 hours, stopping it adds the charge as a line, "total 225000 items [["Karaoke odası",225000]]". A garson who then cancels without a PIN is refused: 403 approval_required, permission siparis.iptal.

Bug, cancel path: same 2-hour session, but the garson cancels while the timer is still running, with no PIN and no reason.
- Result: "CANCEL garson (no pin, no reason): 200 iptal total 0".
- The session stays open: [{"endedAt":null,"itemId":null,"rate":100000}].
- The only audit entry is info level, amount 0, no approver: "#2 boş adisyon kapatıldı". The patron sees an empty order closed, not about 2000 TL of room use thrown away.
- The charge cannot be recovered. A mudur stopping the timer gets 409 order_closed ("önce adisyonu yeniden açın"). Reopening also fails, 409 "Yalnız kapanmış adisyon yeniden açılır", because reopenOrder only accepts 'kapali' orders, not 'iptal'.
- The floor no longer shows the cancelled order.
- The web UI offers "Adisyonu iptal et" whenever the order is editable and paid=0, so this is a normal button in the app, not only an API path.

Bug, day-close path: a kasiyer's manual day close runs closeDay, which treats the itemless room order as empty. It cancels it ("iptal Boş adisyon (gün sonu) total 0"), the room stays running with endedAt null, the Z closes with 200, and the audit is again info level with amount 0. The automatic 05:00 job skips days with any open order, so only the manual close triggers this.

The design clearly means a running room to be billed first: closeOrder, addPayment and the OKC path all call assertNoActiveRoom. cancelOrder and closeDay do not.

Why medium, not high:
- Loss needs either a deliberate cancel by staff, or a Z taken while a karaoke room is running with no food or drink on it. Both are narrow.
- A dishonest waiter could also just never start the timer.
- It does not corrupt the Z's cash balance: collected payments still reconcile.
- The real harm is lost revenue of at least 1000 TL per session (60-minute minimum at the seed rate), plus an approval bypass hidden behind a misleading info-level "empty order" audit entry.

title: Moving every item off a room order closes it as 'birlesti' while its timer runs, so the room charge can never be billed
description: transferItems checks neither assertNoActiveRoom nor whether a room session exists. When all non-voided items leave and the source has no live payments, it sets the source to status 'birlesti'. The room session stays running on that closed order, stopRoom then fails with order_closed, and the target can be paid and closed for only the items. A garson (masa.islem) can let a customer use the karaoke room and then move the drinks to another table, and no room charge reaches any order.
evidence:
source after transfer: status birlesti room {"id":"01M5WCTR7KCG6XFYS7TZ4ZFXFB","startedAt":1793028088051,"endedAt":null,"hourlyRate":100000} total 0
target after transfer: status acik total 28000 room null
room stop on source: 409 {"error":"Adisyon kapalı; oda ücretini yazmak için önce adisyonu yeniden açın","code":"order_closed"}
target paid & closed: true paid 28000

The code means to block this. addPayment and closeOrder both call assertNoActiveRoom, and OKC send is blocked too. The baseline test in the probe shows that paying a room order with a running timer is refused with code room_running. transferItems (server/services/orders.ts:614-683) skips that check. When every non-voided item leaves and there are no live payments, it sets the source to 'birlesti'. mergeOrders moves the room session to the target, but transferItems leaves it behind.

What the probe showed:
- The garson role alone (it has masa.islem by default, shared/permissions.ts:68) can do the transfer with no approver PIN: `TRANSFER by garson (no approver): 200`.
- `SOURCE after: birlesti room {..."endedAt":null,"hourlyRate":100000}` and `TARGET after: acik total 28000 room null`.
- The floor misleads staff. Before the transfer the room table showed `[{"no":2,"roomStartedAt":true}]`. After it showed `FLOOR after: room table orders []`, so the karaoke room looks free while its timer is still running.
- Every recovery path fails:
  - Stopping the timer as mudur: `409 order_closed`. The error message says to reopen the order first.
  - Reopening as patron: `409 "Yalnız kapanmış adisyon yeniden açılır"`, because reopenOrder only accepts 'kapali', not 'birlesti'.
  - Merging the source into the target: `409 order_closed`.
  - Stopping the timer on the target: `404 Çalışan oda sayacı bulunamadı`.
- The target is paid and closed for the drinks only: `TARGET paid: true 28000`.
- The day closes normally: `DAY close: 200 netSales 142000`. The room session stays in the DB with `endedAt:null,itemId:null` and never reaches any order, report or Z. Nothing flags it.

Impact: room time at 1,000 TL/hour (100000 kuruş in the seed) is lost from sales and the Z. A garson can collect the room fee in cash without recording it, which gets around the server-side room_running control. It can also happen by mistake: TransferModal (src/pages/order/TableOps.tsx) lets staff select all items and move them, including with the default 'Aynı masada ayrı hesap' option, with no room warning. The order.transfer and room.start entries are audited, but no alarm is raised.

title: Room timer started while the basket is pending; the device payment then closes the order with the timer still running
description: `sendOrderToDevice` refuses to send while a room timer runs (room_running), because a closed order must not get a room fee later. `startRoom` does not check for a pending device basket, though, and `addExternalPayments` closes the order without `assertNoActiveRoom`. Starting the room after sending and then paying on the device closes the order with an active session. `room/stop` then fails with order_closed, so the room fee is never billed or fiscalized unless a manager reopens the order with approval.
fix: Reject room/start while the order has a pending device basket (assertNoPendingDevice). Also, in addExternalPayments, do not close the order while a room session is active: leave it open and raise an alarm.

title: Room timer can be started and billed on a site-paid online order; the charge can never be collected (rule 7)
description: startRoom and stopRoom do not call assertPosOrder, and moveOrder (orders.ts:555) accepts an online (extPaid) order and rewrites its type to 'masa'. A waiter can move a site-paid order to a karaoke room, or start the timer directly on a QR order placed on a room table. stopRoom then inserts a 1,250 TL 'Karaoke odası' line into the extPaid order and recalcs its total. addPayment refuses extPaid orders, so the charge cannot be taken: the room time is lost revenue and the order now carries a POS amount, which AGENTS.md rule 7 forbids.
fix: Call assertPosOrder(o) in startRoom, stopRoom and moveOrder, or have moveOrder keep the type for laffogato orders and refuse to move them onto an 'oda' table. Close via /orders/:id/close should also refuse extPaid orders.

title: Opening a table that has an open site QR order returns the paid online order, so the waiter cannot add items
description: Online table orders get tableId from siteTableCode. createOrder(type 'masa') without newCheck returns any open order on that table, whatever its source. The FloorPage and ReservationsPage ('geldi') flows call POST /orders {type:'masa', tableId} and get the site-paid laffogato order back. Adding items then fails with 409 online_order, and the reservation's guests and note are silently dropped. transferItems (line 636) already excludes source != 'pos' and extPaid orders; createOrder does not.
fix: In createOrder's existing-order lookup, add `eq(schema.orders.source, 'pos')` and `eq(schema.orders.extPaid, false)` (as transferItems does), so a POS check is opened next to the online order.

title: cancelOrder has no base permission gate: a user with no sales rights cancels another user's empty open order
description: cancelOrder only requires siparis.iptal when there are live (non-fresh) items (approverId = live.length && !allFresh ? need(...) : null). For an order with no sent items, no base permission is checked at all, so POST /api/orders/:id/cancel lets any authenticated user — including a kurye whose only permission is paket.yonet — set another user's freshly-opened table order to status 'iptal'. With sent items the guard correctly blocks a no-sales user (confirmed), so the gap is limited to empty/all-fresh orders, but it still lets staff with zero order permissions mutate order/table state they should not touch.
evidence:
[cancel] kurye perms ["paket.yonet"] -> empty order cancel status 200 order status iptal (FAIL: expected 403)
[cancel] with items, kurye cancel -> 403 approval_required (PASS: guard holds once items are sent)
fix: Add a base needDirect(actor, 'siparis.al') (or 'siparis.iptal') at the top of cancelOrder so cancelling any order requires an order permission, independent of whether it currently has live items.
